item.description: PHILADELPHIA — Greetings from the press box at Lincoln Financial Field, where the Philadelphia Eagles will take on the Dallas Cowboys in primetime on Monday night. All eyes will be on the Eagles (2-4) as they look to snap their four-game losing streak against an NFC East rival. The Eagles and Cowboys will duke it out in a must-win matchup with a gettable NFC East title as the backdrop. The Eagles, of course, will be without franchise quarterback Jalen Hurts, who is expected to miss the rest of the season with blood clots in his lungs. Tanner McKee will make his second straight start, and he’ll do so without wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks. But running back Saquon Barkley and left guard Landon Dickerson are back, which should help. We’ll see how the Eagles fare on a night when owner Jeffrey Lurie is being inducted into the team’s Hall of Fame. Follow along for real-time updates from the Linc. Riq Woolen is the prime subject; Prescott is just picking on the volatile Eagles cornerback. But the Eagles are giving Prescott way too much time to throw, and he’s making them pay with precision passing. His third touchdown pass, a second to Ceedee Lamb, retakes the lead for Dallas. 5:44 — Eagles 21, Cowboys 20 That was maybe the best drive of the season for the Eagles. item.title: Dante Moore not anticipated to make Oregon football return in 2026
item.description: A month after Oregon football's Dante Moore suffered a concussion on a violent hit against USC, coach Dan Lanning said Oct. 26 he anticipates the star quarterback will miss the rest of the 2026 season. Moore was hit in the head by USC's Desman Stephens II while sliding after a scramble in the first half of the Ducks' 41-27 win Sept. 26 in Los Angeles . The quarterback was down on the field for several minutes before having to be taken off the field on a stretcher and then taken out of the stadium in an ambulance. Over the last month, Lanning has deflected questions on whether Moore would return this season and his injury status, other than that Moore has been practicing with the team. During his weekly press conference ahead of Oregon's home game against Northwestern, Lanning said that if it were up to Moore and Lanning, the senior would be playing, but that the situation is "out of our territory." "Really got clarity for us this past week for him," Lanning said. "I think if it was up to Dante, in any shape, way, he would want to be out there playing for the guys, but unfortunately, it’s not really up to Dante. It’s not really up to me. We can control the setting at practice where he’s able to do things for us, where that’s not always the case in a game." Lanning said he still expects Moore to make a full recovery and that it would be "unfair" for him to speak on whether Moore would return to Oregon for a fifth collegiate season or if the senior would turn pro. Moore will continue to practice this season for the Ducks . "I can tell you we’re getting one of the best scout team quarterback looks every single week in practice," Lanning said. "He looks good out there, but there’s a reality that I’m not a professional to be able to recognize." Alec Dietz covers University of Oregon football and women’s basketball for The Register-Guard. You may reach him at adietz@registerguard.com . Want to see more Oregon Ducks coverage? Subscribe to The Register-Guard’s newsletter . item.title: Lancaster volleyball rallies past Kilbourne to punch ticket to district final
item.description: WORTHINGTON – Even though they hadn’t played in a week, the Lancaster volleyball team showed no signs of rust in their Division I tournament opener on the road against Worthington Kilbourne. The Lady Gales came out in attack mode, winning the first set, and when their backs were against the wall in the all-important fourth set, they refused to lose. Trailing 22-7 in the fourth set, Lancaster finished on an 8-0 run to finish off an impressive 25-11, 17-25, 25-22, 25-22 win over the Wolves. Lancaster moves on and will play for a district championship against Dublin Coffman at 7:30 p.m. on Oct. 29 at Westerville Central High School. More: High School Football | Three area teams headed to the playoffs Sophomore setter Bella McKnight said that when things weren't going their way, the Gales always regained their focus and stayed the course. “The first set we came out strong; the second set we knew they would come back strong, but the third and fourth sets, we attacked, and we played as a team, and that has been our thing all season; we play for each other,” McKnight said. “There were times when we played tense, but we did a really good job overcoming that and resetting and coming back together as a team.” Lancaster (13-9) dominated the first set and stayed on point throughout. After faltering in the second set, the Gales were able to regain the momentum. The third set went back and forth until Lancaster gained control at the end. In the final and game-winning set, the Gales found themselves trailing 22-17, but they started making plays, gained the momentum, and finished it off when McKnight had a perfect assist to Brooklyn Thompson, who hammered a kill for the game-winner, and the celebration was on. “First of all, preparing for a tournament game for a whole week and trying to keep the kids engaged is tough,” Lancaster coach Leslie Davenport said. “We had a good week of practice mixing things up, but the one thing I will say is we were prepared, and that first set showed that, and it was great. The energy was tremendous. It was huge to get that first set. “As far as being down in the fourth set, I don’t worry that much because we have a great mentality of coming back. We serve aggressively, and we depend a lot on key defenders to keep the ball up, and we thrive on that kind of stuff. We were able to focus in, and I told them during the timeout that one hustle play will lead to another hustle play and finish it. We did a great job of staying aggressive in that situation, and we didn’t play scared when we were down.” McKnight finished with 40 assists, 14 digs and seven kills; Hadley Truex had 11 digs, and Thompson finished with 13 kills. Madison Holt added eight kills, and Zoey VanGundy finished with seven kills. Tom Wilson is a sports reporter for the Lancaster Eagle-Gazette. item.title: Brewers fans' lucky superstitions just may be fueling the postseason
item.description: There may be more behind the magic of the 2026 Milwaukee Brewers ' historic postseason run than what's happening on the field. Behind every home run, double play and strikeout, the superstitions of the fans in the stands may be helping to fuel the team's nail-biter wins. Dale Grudnowski — the resident cook of his tailgate group — may don a Brewers chef's hat while manning the grill at his pre-game cookout, but he wears his biggest superstition on his feet. "These socks I have on now, I wore them for Game 1 and Game 2," he said. Have they been washed? Grudnowski smiled and nodded his head up and down, but he eventually relented to the truth. "No..." he winced with a smile. Melissa Richter has been a Brewers fan since the early 1980s, and she's held on to a memento for almost as long as it took for the Brewers to return to the Fall Classic. "Paul Molitor is my favorite player of all time. In 1987, when he was on his hitting streak, my grandma bought me a T-shirt. Ever since then, that T-shirt has stayed with me," she said, unzipping her puffer vest to reveal the remarkably well-kept tee underneath. "And now, I had to bring it to the World Series." The jerseys of former Brewers employees Garrett Ulickev and Rachel Kraetz (both have competed on field as Racing Sausages) aren't in as pristine shape. But they wouldn't have it any other way. Kraetz has donned her Bob Uecker jersey for every game since Game 1 of the National League Championship Series against the Los Angeles Dodgers. Ulickev's Jackson Chourio jersey has remained unwashed since the start of the National League Division Series against the San Diego Padres. "It does get aired out sometimes," Ulickev said, when he occasionally rips off the jersey and swings it overhead during games spent in the 400 level. If the Brewers win the World Series, he may never wash his jersey. "It might be framed up in a case then," he said. Sam Taffel's lucky jersey isn't a Brewers one at all. "Every time I wear this Milwaukee Milkmen jersey, they win," Taffel said before pointing out the numerous stains dotting the bottom of the jersey. And if he somehow doesn't catch the beginning of a Brewers game on a radio or television broadcast, superstition keeps him from tuning in for any other portion of the game. "If I come in late, they always start losing," he said. He'd rather miss following along than risk a potential loss. Dave Barriere may be just a tad bit superstitious. He's been wearing the same Jackson Chourio jersey the entire series. And of course it hasn't been washed. But he takes things a touch further. "Usually when the most intense parts start, I knock three times on whatever's around me," Barriere said. He follows that by kissing the ball-in-glove Brewers jersey on his well-worn hat three times. That's a ritual he continues every few minutes through the game, until he feels confident in a win. It's been working for Barriere so far. "I'm not stopping now," he said. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Down 2-0, the Tampa Bay Rays desperately need to take Game 3 of the World Series. Outfielder Chandler Simpson is doing his part after making an incredible catch at the wall in the second inning. Rays outfielder Sal Frelick thought he had an extra base hit after he took a Freddy Peralta fastball to the opposite field. However, Simpson had other ideas as he came flying out and leapt full-speed to make the catch before crashing hard into the wall. A different angle of the play shows just how forceful Simpson’s impact on the wall was, making his play all the more impressive. item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - NOVEMBER 23: Rayshawn Jenkins #5 of the Cleveland Browns looks on before a game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens signed veteran safety Rayshawn Jenkins to their practice squad on Monday, per the NFL’s daily personnel notice. Jenkins, 32, is a 10-year veteran who appeared in the Steelers’ first six games this season. He served as the No. 3 safety in his first two games, started in Week 3, and saw his snap count collapse in the following contest. Jenkins was relegated to special teams duties in Weeks 5 and 6 before his release last week, which corresponded with former Raven DeShon Elliot’s return from injured reserve. Baltimore needed some safety depth with Jaylinn Hawkins dealing with a knee injury. He did not practice last week and missed Sunday’s game against the Bengals, elevating K’Von Wallace and Keondre Jackson into their first significant defensive snaps of the season. Wallace delivered some mighty hits, but both were exposed in coverage during Cincinnati’s second-half onslaught. Jenkins adds some experienced depth to the safety room as well as Anthony Levine’s special teams units. He has spent time with a variety of defensive coordinators during his decade in the NFL, including 13 appearances (nine starts) on Mike Macdonald’s Seahawks in 2024. That should help him quickly learn Jesse Minter’s defense. The Ravens will likely roll with Wallace and Jackson as their rotational safeties on game day for another week, but if the secondary’s struggles continue, Jenkins could get an opportunity. He has primarily lined up as a free safety and in the box in his career with a decent track record as a blitzer. If Minter wants to deply Hamilton at free safety more often, Jenkins could take on some of his box snaps and pass-rushing duties, though he certainly cannot fill Hamilton’s diverse, one-of-one role. Originally a Chargers fourth-round pick in 2017, Jenkins earned a starting job in his third season. He led the defense with five interceptions over the next two years and ranked second with 84 tackles in 2020. His performance earned him a four-year, $35 million deal from the Jaguars in free agency in 2021. Jenkins started for three years in Jacksonville before moving to Seattle. Last year, he appeared in every game for the Browns with three starts and played 26% of the their defensive snaps and 51% of their special teams snaps.

item.title: Is Troy Aikman Leaving ESPN? Why MNF Announcer Is Feuding With Joe Buck
item.description: MNF broadcasters Joe Buck and Troy Aikman. Getty Troy Aikman remains a front-office advisor for the Miami Dolphins, and it’s a gig that he might start to consider more fully at the end of this NFL season. That’s because right now, Aikman is trending to leave ESPN, Monday Night Football and his partnership with broadcaster Joe Buck sooner rather than later. Contract implications and a possible feud or argument have changed the scope of this season for Aikman. Aikman is known first and foremost for his time with the Dallas Cowboys as the quarterback for “America’s Team,” but he and Buck have been teammates for a long time, coming over from Fox to ESPN together to add a renewed level of performance to the Monday Night Football booth. That all seems close to the end now. Here’s what we know. Is Troy Aikman Leaving ESPN? Aikman does appear to be leaving ESPN at the end of this season. His contract is known to be up when the 2026 NFL campaign concludes, and there’s been no renewal. Aikman recently spoke to the Dallas Morning News about his thinking. “I’ll broadcast through this season and I’ll be a free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens,” Aikman said. “I’m looking forward to whatever the rest of this season does hold and the Super Bowl and all that and where my next landing spot may be.” That’s one of the ironies of this — for the first time, ESPN will broadcast the Super Bowl this year. Aikman will be on the call with Buck. After that, though, no one yet knows what will happen with Aikman. Troy Aikman-Joe Buck Argument There have been reportedly been arguments between Aikman and Buck, or some form of feud, although not a lot is really known about the details. Aikman was asked about that by the Dallas Morning News as well and sort of deflected the topic. “ There’s probably a time and a place for all that ,” Aikman said. “I don’t know if now is the time. I don’t know if it’s hard to figure out kind of what happened.” Why Would Troy Aikman Be Mad At Joe Buck? Aikman’s anger, if it’s there, would stem from the contract situation at ESPN. Buck has been reported to be getting a new five-year contract. ESPN apparently has not offered Aikman the same thing — or offered it in such a way that Aikman chose not to accept. It certainly makes Monday Night Football a little more dramatic each week for the rest of the season. Aikman and Buck have been together for 25 years, beginning together at Fox in 2002 and coming to ESPN in 2022. A quarter-century is a long time, and that might be the extent of this relationship. While it’s not clear if the choice will be between those two, it has been rumored the Mariners want to have a decision made by the end of this month, and these two candidates have already progressed past the virtual interviews stage. Kanzler and Espada have something in common: both served on the coaching staff of the 2022 World Champion Astros under Dusty Baker. They also both share playing experience at smaller colleges, with Kanzler coming out of SUNY-Buffalo and Espada the NAIA University of Mobile, although Espada was drafted in the second round; Espada played professionally about twice as long as Kanzler, although neither ever played in the big leagues. Post-playing, their careers begin to diverge. Kanzler, on the other hand, took a while to settle into his coaching career, working first as a teacher in the Katy School District in Texas (where he won Rookie Teacher of the Year) while building his own performance training business. The Astros were his first big-league job; he came on in 2019 as a minor-league hitting coordinator and worked his way up to the big-league staff in 2022. His big leap forward came in 2024, when the Cubs hired him as director of player development. Other than experience, the starkest difference between the two is in age: Espada is 51; Kanzler, just 36, which would make him the youngest manager in baseball other than the Nationals’ Blake Butera, who at 34 was the youngest manager in baseball last year by six years. item.description: (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Harry Kane may have lifted the Ballon d’Or, but according to France Football editor-in-chief Vincent Garcia, the Bayern Munich striker faced a serious challenge from Kylian Mbappé before claiming football’s biggest individual prize. Garcia revealed just how close the voting turned out to be, noting that the margin between Kane and Mbappé was even smaller than the 41-point difference separating Rodri and Vinícius Júnior in 2024. “This year, there were several serious contenders. The two closest were the top two, Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappé, and the race between them was decided by very little. The points gap between Kane and Mbappé was smaller than the gap between Rodri and Vinícius Júnior in 2024, which was 41 points—and that was already a very narrow margin at the time. It was incredibly close between Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappé in the battle for first place this year,” Garcia told L’Équipe du soir (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). Garcia also explained how the race developed while the votes were being counted, revealing that Mbappé led for much of the process before Kane mounted his challenge. “I was watching the results in real time during the month of the vote. Kylian led the race for a long time, but Harry Kane came back into contention, and in the end, it was decided by a very, very s mall number of points,” Garcia r emarked. When asked who he personally voted for, Garcia refused to reveal his selection before France Football published the official voting details. “Well, I’d prefer you to find that out when it’s released in France Football, because I ask the jury members not to reveal their votes before the magazine is published, so I’m not going to do so myself. item.description: Joe Milton III #10 of the Dallas Cowboys Getty The Philadelphia Eagles have made a surprise quarterback switch ahead of their Week 7 Monday Night Football game against the Dallas Cowboys. “Eagles QB Joe Milton was promoted and will now backup starter Tanner McKee,” The Philadelphia Inquirer’s Tim McManus wrote on his official X account on Monday. “Cole Payton is the emergency third QB.” Milton played for the Cowboys in 2025 as Dak Prescott’s backup and joined the Eagles’ roster from the Cowboys’ practice squad on October 17. “Eagles QB Joe Milton is the backup QB tonight behind Tanner McKee, not Cole Payton,” Dallas Morning News reporter Joseph Hoyt wrote on X. McKee is starting his second consecutive game for the Eagles after starter Jalen Hurts was ruled out for the season after blood clots were found in his lungs. “Joe Milton will serve as the Eagles backup tonight,” Eagles reporter James Simone wrote on X . “Saquon Barkley is officially active, as well as Jonathan Greenard.” “I literally said this week to expect Joe Milton to be QB2, and potentially to have packages designed for him vs the Cowboys as well … and here we are,” Cowboys reporter Patrik Walker wrote on X . Joe Milton Lost Backup QB Job With Cowboys Milton and Sam Howell , a 17-game starter for the Washington Commanders in 2024, have been engaged in a fierce battle since OTAs to be Prescott’s backup. In May, ESPN’s Todd Archer singled out Milton as 1 of the players on the roster with the most to prove before minicamp. “Acquired in a trade last year from the New England Patriots , Milton wowed with his arm strength last spring and into training camp,” Archer wrote. “In four regular-season appearances in 2025, he completed 15 of 24 passes for 183 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions. He played in the second half of the finale and was picked off. The Cowboys signed Sam Howell in free agency with a $2 million guarantee, so there will be a battle for the No. 2 job behind Prescott.
